content:
Hi Diana

Is the configuration in Thunderbird for Android definately setup to use pop. Can you share a screen shot from it's settings page

  • Settings > account name > fetching mail > incoming server.

Pop3 connections by default delete emails from the server unless you've specifically configured your provider webmail settings and apps to retain them on the server.

The following scenario / setup could create the effect you describe.

  • Thunderbird for Android using Imap.
  • TB Desktop using Pop.
  1. TB Android downloads your email (imap)
  2. TB Desktop (or other pop client) downloads the email and deletes it from server (pop default)
  3. TB Android synchronises it's view to match the server.
  4. TB Android deletes its copy of the email because its no longer available on the server.

Have you logged onto your providers webmail and checked if the email is within it's inbox. Don't assume it is because your email is available in Thunderbird desktop.

content:
I can reproduce similar UI behavior on recent Android versions, and it does look more like a visual/UI issue than an intended feature. If the status bar consistently turns completely black only after selecting a message, while the rest of the interface behaves normally, it may be related to how Thunderbird handles edge-to-edge rendering or system bar colors on Android 15 devices such as the **Pixel 9 Pro**.

We've encountered similar UI rendering quirks while testing HD Streamz on newer Pixel devices, where status bar appearance changed unexpectedly due to system UI handling. It would be interesting to know whether this also occurs on the latest Thunderbird build from the Play Store or only in the F-Droid version.
